Mika Tan: Hi all, first-week question: I'm validating an SSH-proxy'd devbox that forwards requests through our internal NAT for hosted API calls. Should I use sandbox keys or request a hosted ephemeral key to get realistic behavior?
Omar Ruiz: Welcome Mika! If you need production kernel behavior / exact latency, use a hosted ephemeral key. Sandbox can diverge (smaller models, diff quant). For purely functional tests sandbox is fine.
Mika Tan: The proxy will make requests from the shared CI NAT; is that ok for a hosted window?
Priya Rao: Yes — we can map the shared CI NAT to an ops rule. When filing the ticket include: "source: shared-CI-NAT", time window, expected total requests, batch vs streaming, and model. Example: "window 2026-03-29 10:00-10:30 UTC, ~2k non-stream requests, model: redwood-medium, source: shared-CI-NAT".
Mika Tan: Great. Any tips about header propagation or long-lived connections through the SSH proxy? I ran into 401s once when the proxy reused connections.
Omar Ruiz: Two gotchas: 1) If the proxy multiplexes connections your key rotation may not be seen until reconnect; plan for reconnects on auth failure. 2) Streaming over an SSH tunnel can be sensitive to MTU/timeouts; increase keepalive on the tunnel.
Mika Tan: How do I check key type and expiry from the CLI before I start?
Priya Rao: Quick check:
```
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/keys/me | jq '.key_type, .expires_at'
```
It prints "hosted" or "sandbox" and expiry for ephemeral keys.
Mika Tan: If I get 429s during the run, what's the recommended immediate action?
Omar Ruiz: First: check Console -> Usage -> API Keys for per-key QPS and recent 429s. If it's a single-key cap, rotate to the secondary ephemeral key or backoff. For CI runs, we usually implement exponential backoff with jitter (base 100ms, max 2s).
DevOps Bot: Tip: you can emulate 429s locally with header `X-Test-Force-429: after=10` to exercise client retries. Do not use that for perf numbers.
Finance Bot: Reminder: hosted ephemeral windows outside onboarding credits bill the project. Include billing owner in OPS ticket if estimated >$50.
Mika Tan: Filed OPS-5205: "Request ephemeral hosted key for shared-CI-NAT, 2026-03-29 10:00-10:30 UTC, ~2k non-streaming requests, model redwood-medium". CC @Priya Rao.
Priya Rao: Received OPS-5205. I'll approve the window and add the CI NAT mapping. Keys will appear in Console -> API Keys -> Ephemeral. I'll post when active.
Mika Tan: Thanks all! I'll run a small smoke first and then the full run.
Omar Ruiz: If you want, request two ephemeral keys so you can rotate mid-run without downtime.
Mika Tan: Will do. Appreciate the help :thumbsup:
